subject: Invoice splitback and VAT allocation for AWS listing #A-9921
messages:
From: Atlas Data Billing <billing@atlasdata.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 08:14:00 -0400
Subject: Unexpected invoice split on AWS listing A-9921

Hi Marissa,

We received our May invoice via AWS Marketplace and noticed the charge against listing A-9921 appears split across two entities (Atlas EU GmbH and Atlas Global Inc.) with VAT applied differently. Attached is the vendor invoice (atlas_invoice_202505.pdf) and the AWS line items AWS provided. Can you help trace how Redwood routed the usage for that listing in May? Our finance team needs a clean VAT breakdown to claim a credit.

Quick facts:
- Invoice total: EUR 12,420.00
- Split: EUR 9,150 (Atlas EU GmbH) | EUR 3,270 (Atlas Global Inc.) per AWS lines
- We expected full allocation to Atlas EU GmbH (our EU entity) per the marketplace contract.

Could you confirm whether any ledger remapping or reproration happened on Redwood's side during the May billing window? If you can provide a CSV with usage-to-entity mapping and any signed PO/override that caused a reproration, that would be ideal.

Thanks —
Daniel Park
Billing Lead, Atlas Data
attachments: atlas_invoice_202505.pdf, aws_lineitems_202505.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <billing@atlasdata.com>, AWS Marketplace Seller Support <aws-marketplace-seller-support@amazon.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Unexpected invoice split on AWS listing A-9921

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. We've pulled the initial telemetry and there's an atypical reproration event on May 29 that looks like it re-attributed a subset of metered usage to Atlas Global Inc. rather than Atlas EU GmbH.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll run a canonical usage export for listing A-9921 for May and map token/byte-level allocations to the entity tag we use in settlement (deliverable: CSV).
- Karthik, can you extract the batch-level mapping and confirm whether any manual remediation or merchant-mapping rule matched on 2025-05-29? Please include the KV cache timestamps if relevant.
- Jonas, please check if any marketplace routing override was triggered from the marketplace connector (we had a transient retry/batch split that week).

I'm attaching a Redwood evidence template (redwood_evidence_template.xlsx) — please paste the export into tab 'usage_mapping' and include any signed PO or override IDs in the header. We'll reconcile and propose a corrective credit for the misallocated EUR 3,270 if we confirm internal re-routing.

We aim to get this to you by EOD Monday.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Partner Ops, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — partner-ops@redwood.com
attachments: redwood_evidence_template.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jun 2025 09:48:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected invoice split on AWS listing A-9921

Marissa / Jonas — quick findings from the runtime logs.

Summary:
- On 2025-05-29T03:12:10Z we started a retry window for the listing where the marketplace connector re-chunked a long-running stream into two batches due to a partial network timeout with the AWS connector. The batch id was BAT-7721.
- The batch re-chunk logic currently inherits the entity tag from the first successful chunking pass; in this case, the fallback mapping incorrectly pointed at Atlas Global Inc.'s legacy entity token (entity_id: atl-global-01) for ~18% of tokens in that day's window.
- No manual remediation was applied by infra; this was an automated fallback path.

I've exported per-token attribution for the May 24–30 window and attached the metering-pulse-log (metering-pulse-log-202505.xml). The CSV redwood_evidence_template.xlsx has been populated under 'usage_mapping' with three columns: timestamp | token_count | attributed_entity. You'll see the contiguous range 2025-05-29T03:12:10Z–03:42:27Z where ~3,270 EUR worth of usage was credited to atl-global-01.

Suggested fix: propose a corrective settlement entry against the May batch to reassign those tokens to Atlas EU GmbH and request a marketplace credit for the misattributed portion. We'll also patch the fallback mapping to prefer explicit entity_id in the chunk headers to avoid defaulting to legacy tokens.

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Ingest & Metering
attachments: metering-pulse-log-202505.xml

Hi Marissa / Karthik / Jonas — thanks for the fast triage and the detailed log export. I reviewed the populated template and the XML fragments Karthik sent. This aligns with what our accounting team found.

Atlas is willing to accept a corrective settlement for the EUR 3,270 if Redwood can:
1) Submit a marketplace settlement correction request to AWS Marketplace with the per-line reallocation (we need the AWS request id for our records).
2) Provide an EU VAT breakdown showing the original VAT charge on the EUR 3,270 and the corrected VAT liability (so we can issue a VAT credit and re-file the reclaim).
3) Confirm timelines: we need the request submitted by Jun 20 so our month-end close can reflect the credit in Q2.

If you want, we can sign a short SLA amendment that documents the corrective-path timelines; I'm including a DocuSign link for a one-off acknowledgement (https://docusign.com/s/XXX-redwood-atlas-corrective).

Please let me know the AWS correction request id once submitted and the expected date for the VAT breakdown.

Regards,
Daniel Park
